newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares rise at noon as Shanghai surges.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares rise at noon as Shanghai surges.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index advanced during the morning session on Monday, boosted by a sharp rise in Shanghai's B share market, brokers said.
The Shenzhen B index gained 3.23 points or 1.83 percent to 179.50 on turnover of HK$86.6 million.
Shanghai's B share index soared 5.690 points or 6.24 percent to 96.909 by noon with investors scrambling to buy blue chips and Pudong real estate related shares, brokers said.
"The Shenzhen market jumped in tandem with its Shanghai counterpart," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Analysts said they expect Shenzhen B shares to extend gains during the afternoon session due to good sentiment.
"Shenzhen will follow suit if Shanghai remains bullish," the J&A analyst said.
Steep rises in Shenzhen and Shanghai's domestic A share markets, despite Beijing's announcement of plans to boost A share issues, also helped B shares to advance, brokers said.
Shenzhen's A share index climbed 15.01 points or 3.07 percent to 504.23 on heavy turnover of 8.32 billion yuan.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission, the country's top securities watchdog, on Monday announced a new five billion yuan quota, in addition to the existing 10 billion yuan, for new share issues in 1997 or later.
Analysts said they viewed the announcement as a move to cool down China's stock markets, since new issues would absorb funds.
"But A shares firmed as investors have digested the news," a second analyst said.
However, analysts warned that an overly speculative market and continuous rises could trigger more government measures to cool the markets.
Shenzhen Tellus Machinery was the sharpest gainer in Shenzhen's B share market, soaring HK$0.18 or 5.63 percent to HK$3.38 on volume of 510,940 shares.
Brokers said the surge was sparked by hopes that the firm's new shareholder would drag Tellus into the black in 1997 after the company posted a net loss of 187.55 million yuan for 1996.

Tellus announced last Wednesday that state firm Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Development (Group) Co had bought 159.59 million state shares, accounting for 72.4 percent of Tellus's outstanding shares, from local government-backed Shenzhen Investment & Management Co.
